title: 第5章 建立据点第6章 领地探巡与营地新貌
slug: 穿越自带炼妖壶桀桀顷刻炼化
content_zh:
第2天，罗恩在橡木城内购买了大量的粮食与物资，又将农奴购买回来，就趁着早上急忙赶路了。
三天后，罗恩终于带领着车队到达了领地。
夏末的风带着草木的腥气，拂过罗恩的脸颊。
他勒住马缰，望着眼前这片延展至天际的荒原，绿水河的支流像一条银带，在远处的低洼处蜿蜒，岸边的芦苇丛密得能藏住一头麋鹿。
“大人，营地就选在那片高地上。”
劳恩·洋葱的声音带着风尘，他刚带着两名卫兵绕着周边勘察了一圈，指着东北方一处隆起的土坡。
“坡顶平坦，能望出去两公里，坡下有片硬土，打桩稳当，离水源也近。”
罗恩点头，策马向土坡走去。马蹄踏过及腰的野草，惊起一群蚂蚱。
土坡确实是块好地方，背靠着一道天然的浅崖，崖壁上长满了耐旱的荆棘，刚好能挡住后方的视线。坡前是开阔的草甸，任何动静都瞒不过岗哨。
“佩林。”
罗恩翻身下马，将缰绳递给侍从。
“让农奴们清理出最少方圆200米的空地，再带队去砍树，做个临时围栏。
告诉他们，天黑前圈不出样子，今晚的黑麦面包就减半。”
佩林连忙应着，拿出羊皮纸开始给农奴们分派任务。好在罗恩从家族带来不少人，不然还真凑不够这么多管事。
三十名卫兵分成两队，一队守在坡下警戒，一队跟着农奴们监工。
他们可不敢真让农奴慢悠悠地磨蹭，这荒原上的危险，谁也说不准什么时候会冒出来。
罗恩没闲着。他带着劳恩洋葱和哈特小扁豆，沿着绿水河支流往上游走。
河水不算深，刚没过马腿，水底的鹅卵石清晰可见，偶尔有银色的小鱼窜过。
走了约莫两里地，劳恩突然勒住马：
“大人，您看那边。”

河对岸的灌木丛里，露出几截朽木，像是被遗弃的木屋残骸。
罗恩眯起眼，让哈特留在原地，自己和劳恩蹚水过去。残骸周围长满了半人高的野草，显然已经荒废了很久，墙角还堆着些破烂的陶碗。
“是以前的开拓民留下的？”罗恩踢了踢一块朽木，木屑簌簌往下掉。
“多半是。”
劳恩捡起一把锈迹斑斑的镰刀。
“看这腐朽程度，少说空了三四年。可能是被野兽袭扰，也可能是……没撑过冬天。”
罗恩没说话，目光扫过四周。
这片河岸的土壤比别处肥沃些，草丛里还能看到零星的野麦，若是开垦出来，建立一个黑麦农庄，收成应该不差。
他在心里记下这个位置，转身往回走。
回到营地时，围栏已经立起了大半。
几百根小腿粗的圆木深深砸进土里，杆与杆之间用削尖的树枝交叉固定，虽然简陋，却透着股结实劲儿。
农奴们正用斧头砍着多余的枝桠，铁匠铺的炉火已经升起，叮叮当当的敲打声在荒原上回荡，他们在赶制门闩和栅栏的锁扣。
罗恩站在坡顶往下看。
农奴们分成几拨正往围栏外搬运石块，佩林说要在围栏外堆一道矮石墙，防着野兽冲撞。
迪克被安排去清点物资，正蹲在一辆马车旁，拿着账本核对麻袋上的标记，眉头皱得像个疙瘩。
“哈特。”
“你带五个人，去西边的树林看看，能不能找到适合做屋顶的树皮，再带些农奴砍些直溜的树干回来，晚上得把卫兵的哨塔搭起来。”
content_en:
On the second day, Ron bought a large amount of food and supplies in Oak City, bought the serfs back, and hurried on his way in the morning.
Three days later, Ron finally led the convoy to the territory.
The late summer wind carried the smell of vegetation and brushed Ron's cheek.
He reined in his horse and looked at the wilderness stretching to the horizon before him. The tributaries of the Green Water River were like a silver ribbon, winding in the low-lying areas in the distance. The reeds on the shore were so thick that they could hide an elk.
"Sir, the camp will be on that high ground."
Lawn Onion's voice was filled with dust. He had just led two guards to survey the surrounding area and pointed to a raised earth slope in the northeast.
"The top of the slope is flat, and you can see out for two kilometers. There is a piece of hard soil at the bottom of the slope. The piling is stable and it is close to the water source."
Ron nodded and rode towards the slope. The horse's hooves trampled the waist-high weeds, startling a group of grasshoppers.
The slope is indeed a good place, backed by a natural shallow cliff. The cliff is covered with drought-resistant thorns, just enough to block the view behind. In front of the slope is an open meadow, and any movement cannot be hidden from the sentry.
"Palin."
Ron dismounted and handed the reins to the attendant.
“Let the serfs clear an open space of at least 200 meters in radius, and then lead a team to cut down trees and build a temporary fence.
Tell them that if they can't make a circle before dark, the rye bread tonight will be halved. "
Perrin responded quickly, took out the parchment and began assigning tasks to the serfs. Fortunately, Ron brought a lot of people from his family, otherwise he wouldn't be able to manage so many people.
Thirty guards were divided into two teams. One team was on guard down the slope, and the other team followed the serfs to supervise the work.
They didn't dare to let the serfs take their time. No one could tell when the dangers in the wilderness would appear.
Ron was busy. He took Lawn onions and Hart's lentils upstream along a tributary of the Greenwater River.
The river is not too deep, just below the horse's legs. The pebbles on the bottom of the water are clearly visible, and occasionally there are small silver fish scurrying by.
After walking about two miles, Lawn suddenly reined in his horse:
"Sir, look over there."
A few pieces of rotten wood were exposed in the bushes on the other side of the river, like the remains of an abandoned wooden house.
Ron narrowed his eyes and asked Hart to stay where he was while he and Ron waded through the water. The wreckage was surrounded by weeds half as tall as a man. It had obviously been abandoned for a long time, and there were some broken pottery bowls piled in the corner.
"Is it left by the former pioneers?" Ron kicked a piece of rotten wood, and sawdust fell down.
"Mostly."
Raun picked up a rusty scythe.
"Looking at the degree of decay, it has been empty for at least three or four years. It may have been attacked by wild beasts, or it may have... not survived the winter."
Ron said nothing and glanced around.
The soil on this river bank is more fertile than elsewhere, and sporadic wild wheat can be seen in the grass. If it is cultivated and a rye farm is built, the harvest should be good.
He made a mental note of this location, turned around and walked back.
When we got back to the camp, the fence was mostly up.
Hundreds of calf-thick logs were smashed deeply into the soil, and sharpened branches were fixed between the poles. Although they were simple, they showed strong strength.
The serfs were chopping down the extra branches with axes. The fire in the blacksmith shop had been lit. The sound of clanking hammering echoed in the wilderness. They were working on the door bolts and the locks of the fence.
Ron stood at the top of the slope and looked down.
The serfs were divided into several groups and were carrying stones outside the fence. Palin said that a low stone wall should be built outside the fence to prevent wild animals from charging.
Dick was assigned to count the supplies. He was squatting next to a carriage, holding a ledger to check the marks on the sacks, his brows furrowed like a pimple.
"Hart."
"Take five people and go to the woods to the west to see if you can find bark suitable for roofing. Then bring back some serfs to cut some straight tree trunks. You have to put up the guard tower at night."
